Subject: Intermittent 5xx/timeouts during warmup window (need SLA guidance)

Hi Soojin,

We observed a spike of 503s and long tail timeouts for inference calls during a deploy this morning. Impacted window (UTC): ~2029-07-01 06:10 - 06:22. ~3% of requests returned 503 and an additional ~8% had response times between 5-12s (our median before/after was ~120ms).

This affected our critical checkout flow for ~12 minutes and matches the volume of traffic we'd expect in a typical morning peak. Can you confirm whether this qualifies for an SLO credit and what evidence you need from us? We can share request IDs, sample traces, and the deploy artifact id.

Quick context: we were rolling a blue/green deploy at ~06:05 UTC. We saw a gradual increase in 5xx starting at 06:10 and resolving by ~06:22 when requests returned to baseline.

Please advise on next steps (evidence pull, postmortem, timeline).

Thanks,
Marc

Quick update from infra ops after correlating telemetry: we pulled the traces and host metrics for 06:00-06:30 UTC. Findings summary:

- Root cause signal: autoscaler warmup + shard rehydration delay. During the blue/green swap, several model shards started cold and KV cache synchronizations coincided with our request burst.
- Error surface: ~12-minute degradation window from 2029-07-01T06:10:05Z to 2029-07-01T06:22:30Z. 503s appear to be transient failures from shard readiness checks failing before fallback completed.
- Impact quant: ~3.1% 5xx, additional ~7.8% p75-95 inflated to 5–12s.
- Cause note: a regression in a recent autoscaler throttle-change patch allowed simultaneous rehydration operations in a limited subset of instances, causing temporary resource contention.

I've attached the pulled artifacts (trace_bundle_0701.tar.gz) and a KV-cache heatmap (kv-cache-heatmap-0701.png). The trace bundle has request ids that map to PineBank samples.

Preliminary SLO eligibility: looks like a service-caused availability delta. From the contract definition (availability measured by 5xx and timeouts per minute), this event looks eligible for a proportional remedial credit. Need legal/CS confirmation on the exact credit calc (Neha).

Next steps:
- Soojin to confirm customer-facing statement and credit proposal.
- Engineering will do a root-cause postmortem (timeline: initial RCA within 5 business days, full RCA + mitigation plan in 10 business days).

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marc — thanks for your patience. Below is a short, customer-facing summary and our proposed next steps.

Summary of verification:
- Confirmed degraded interval: 2029-07-01T06:10:05Z through 2029-07-01T06:22:30Z (approx. 12 minutes).
- Cause: autoscaler warmup + shard rehydration race leading to temporary readiness failures and elevated latency. Engineering has attached traces and a heatmap for your review.
- Impact: ~3.1% 5xx and ~7.8% elevated tail latencies during the window; baseline restored after 06:22 UTC.

Proposed remediation / customer options:
1) Pro-rated credit: We propose a credit apportionment for the affected interval. Calculation: (12 minutes / total monthly minutes) * monthly service fee. We will provide the exact dollar amount once billing confirms the proration (I expect a figure back within 24 hours).
2) Postmortem: Our engineering team will produce an initial RCA in 5 business days and a full mitigation plan within 10 business days. We propose a 30-minute postmortem call this week to walk through the timeline and planned mitigations — available slots: Tue 07/02 14:00-15:00 UTC or Wed 07/03 10:00-11:00 UTC.

Attachments included: trace_bundle_0701.tar.gz (redacted traces), kv-cache-heatmap-0701.png

If you'd like us to escalate the credit calculation or fast-track the RCA, say the word and I'll loop in our billing/legal.

Would you accept the proposed credit path and the postmortem call on Tue 07/02 14:00 UTC?

Best,
Soojin
